resolutions.headline: Yes: fairly renormalized to one price source at the latest common inception, Self-Directed (+2.92%) beats every Brain in every window tested, and the gap is almost entirely allocation (a defensive tilt into a risk-off tape), not the Brains' churn.
resolutions.answer:
MEASUREMENT CONSTRAINT (load-bearing): the latest common inception is Self-Directed's first fill on 2026-06-23, and ALL parquet price sources in the macro repo end 2026-06-26. So the only fairly-measurable common window is 3 trading days (06-23 to 06-26). Fills after 06-26 (autonomous/heavyweight/hk trade through 07-01; flagship/etf/china through 06-29/30) CANNOT be marked to a real price and are excluded from the head-to-head. The books' own account.json current_price fields mark to 07-01, but that is the bot's self-reported price, not the mandated single source, so I did not use it for the comparison.

PRICE SOURCE: yahoo data/yahoo/*.parquet close (dividend-adjusted) primary; where a name is absent I fell back, in order, to macro data/baskets/ohlcv (US single-names), data/china_stocks, data/hk_stocks, all same vintage, all ending 06-26. Names with NO series anywhere (6 flagship small-caps at inception, SGOV, MCY, 2-4 heavyweight names) are HELD FLAT at last fill price (NAV-neutral) rather than dropped to zero. Markable NAV at inception: self_directed/china/hk = 100%; autonomous 90.6%, flagship 89.7%, etf 85.1%, heavyweight 76.5% (its number is the softest).

RESULT, every book renormalized to $1.00 at 2026-06-23 close, total return 06-23 to 06-26:
  self_directed  +2.923%   maxDD  0.00%   turnover  99%   (100% markable)
  heavyweight    +0.754%   maxDD -1.97%   turnover 278%
  etf            -0.016%   maxDD -0.92%   turnover 161%
  autonomous     -0.465%   maxDD -2.02%   turnover  81%
  flagship       -0.493%   maxDD -1.71%   turnover  98%
  china          -0.481% (CNY, FX caveat)  maxDD -0.48%  turnover 113%
  hk             -3.013% (HKD, FX caveat)  maxDD -3.32%  turnover 114%
  SPY benchmark  -0.626%

DOES SELF-DIRECTED BEAT EVERY BRAIN? Yes, and it beats SPY too. Margins vs Self-Directed (USD books): flagship -3.42pp, autonomous -3.39pp, etf -2.94pp, heavyweight -2.17pp. china/hk are local-currency (CNY/HKD) so not directly comparable in USD, but both are negative in local terms while SD is +2.9%. Self-Directed has ZERO drawdown over the window; every Brain has a negative maxDD.

ROBUSTNESS: the ranking is invariant to inception choice. Testing inception 06-22 / 06-23 / 06-24 (all to 06-26), Self-Directed wins by +5.7 / +3.4 / +2.4pp respectively over the best Brain, and never loses in any window.

HOW MUCH IS TURNOVER/CHURN vs ALLOCATION? Almost all allocation. Frozen day-1 buy-and-hold (freeze inception positions, no trading) vs actual: flagship frozen -0.382% vs actual -0.493% (churn drag -0.11pp); autonomous frozen -0.344% vs actual -0.465% (churn -0.12pp); etf frozen -0.457% vs actual -0.016% (churn +0.44pp, helped); heavyweight frozen -0.007% vs actual +0.754% (churn +0.76pp, helped). So churn is a small effect (~0.1-0.8pp) and in etf/heavyweight it actually HELPED over this window. The 2.4-3.4pp deficit is the allocation itself: the Brains hold SMH/XLK/MTUM/semis-momentum (SMH -1.68% over the window) while Self-Directed holds XLU/XLV/XLF/XLP. Leg decomposition of Self-Directed's +2.923%: XLV +5.36% (contrib +1.61pp), XLU +2.51% (contrib +1.25pp), XLP +1.18% (+0.12pp), XLF -0.58% (-0.06pp). It is a defensive-vs-momentum factor win during a 3-day risk-off tape.

BOTTOM LINE for the customer's framing: the outperformance is REAL as measured, but it is a 3-day, factor-timing artifact of a defensive allocation catching a risk-off window, NOT demonstrated skill over a meaningful horizon. The books are 8-12 days old and price data only supports 3 common days. This is an N-of-3-day result. The honest verdict: Self-Directed's edge over this window is real and allocation-driven, but the sample is far too short to conclude durable superiority.
resolutions.method: Wrote /tmp/mm_reaudit/recon.py. For each book, replayed fills.jsonl from account.json starting_nav (cash) with zero positions, applied every fill (buy: shares+, cash-value; sell: shares-, cash+value) up to each mark date, then marked surviving positions to a single price source: yahoo data/yahoo close (dividend-adjusted) primary, falling back to data/baskets/ohlcv, data/china_stocks, data/hk_stocks (all end 2026-06-26). Renormalized each book's NAV to $1.00 at 2026-06-23 (latest common inception = self_directed first fill). Computed total return, max drawdown, turnover (sum abs(fill value) / avg NAV). Unmarkable names held flat at last fill price to avoid phantom losses. Allocation-vs-selection = frozen day-1 hold (freeze inception positions, mark to end) vs actual replay. Sensitivity-tested inception at 06-22/23/24. FX: china/hk reported in local currency (CNY/HKD) with caveat, not converted.
evidence: data/portfolio/self_directed/fills.jsonl: 5 fills all dated 2026-06-23, queued=true, buying XLU 500k / XLV 300k / XLF 100k / XLP 100k = $1.0M; account.json inception_date 2026-06-22, starting_nav 1000000, cash 0.0 -> book is a static 4-ETF buy-and-hold, 100% price-coverable in yahoo

Price coverage: yahoo/*.parquet is only 216 curated files; 35/41 flagship names, 22/26 heavyweight names, and ALL china/hk names are absent from yahoo. Union with data/baskets/ohlcv + data/china_stocks + data/hk_stocks closes the gap to 6 flagship / 1 etf / 1 autonomous / 2-4 heavyweight unmarkable names. All four sources' last row = 2026-06-26 (verified via df.index.max()).

recon.py output over 06-23->06-26: self_directed +2.923%, heavyweight +0.754%, etf -0.016%, autonomous -0.465%, flagship -0.493%, china -0.481% CNY, hk -3.013% HKD, SPY -0.626%. Self-Directed maxDD 0.00% (monotone up: 1.0000/1.0081/1.0149/1.0292); every Brain has negative maxDD.

Allocation-vs-selection (frozen D1 hold vs actual): flagship -0.382 vs -0.493 (churn -0.11pp); autonomous -0.344 vs -0.465 (-0.12pp); etf -0.457 vs -0.016 (+0.44pp); heavyweight -0.007 vs +0.754 (+0.76pp). Churn is small and in two books positive; the multi-point deficit is allocation.

Self-Directed leg decomposition (yahoo div-adj close 06-23->06-26): XLV +5.362%, XLU +2.507%, XLP +1.183%, XLF -0.575% -> weighted +2.923%. Contrast SMH -1.678% (the Brains' core momentum holding) and SPY -0.626%. Defensive-over-momentum factor win.

Window sensitivity: inception 06-22/06-23/06-24 all to 06-26 -> Self-Directed +2.9/+2.9/+2.1% and wins every window; best Brain never catches it (closest is heavyweight +0.754% at 06-23, still -2.17pp behind and carrying -1.97% DD with only 76.5% of NAV markable).

Turnover: heavyweight 278%, etf 161%, china 113%, hk 114% of avg NAV over a 3-day window (heavyweight buys total $3.12M sells $2.22M on a $1M book) confirms the Brains rotate heavily; Self-Directed turnover 99% is the single day-1 build with zero subsequent trading.
resolutions.implications: Confirms RC6 (the outperforming defensive book is invisible to learning) is pointing at a REAL in-window edge, not a measurement mirage: over the only fairly-comparable 3 days, Self-Directed's XLU/XLV/XLF/XLP beats every Brain by 2.2-3.4pp and beats SPY, with zero drawdown. But it recasts the magnitude: the win is a defensive-vs-momentum FACTOR TILT catching a risk-off tape, and it is nearly all ALLOCATION (churn contributes only ~0.1-0.8pp and in etf/heavyweight actually helped). This sharpens the fix priority: the deficit is the Brains' allocation (RC2/RC5 hardcoded momentum/semis tilt with no defensive rotation), NOT their turnover, so throttling churn will not close the gap; adding a defensive/contrarian allocation seat (RC1/RC5) would. Crucial caveat for ranking: this is an N-of-3-trading-day result on 8-12-day-old books with price data ending 06-26; it CANNOT support a durable-superiority claim. The correct next step is not to crown Self-Directed but to (a) extend the price source past 06-26 (the missing site/stockdata / fresh yahoo pull) so the 07-01 books can be fairly marked, and (b) re-run this exact harness weekly. Any leaderboard shown to the user must carry the '3 common days, allocation-driven, not skill' label or it will overstate the defensive book.

resolutions.headline: Wiring sector_cycles.json into the bot as a Peak/Topping veto is NOT worth it — the veto lowers CAGR (8.2%→4.8%) and Sharpe (0.61→0.47) with negligible drawdown benefit; the phase signal has real but weak forward power (Trough best, Peak worst) that does not survive translation into the bot's top-RS leadership rule.
resolutions.answer:
RECOMMENDATION: Do NOT build W2 as a cycle-phase VETO on the leadership sleeve. The phase does carry mild forward-return information, but a Peak/Topping veto degrades the strategy, and a Peak+Downturn veto is just another de-gross-to-cash lever (RC5), not alpha.

PART A — does phase carry forward-return power? Weakly, yes, directionally correct. Pooled 1,444 sector-month observations (2015-2026), forward returns by phase:
- Trough (Bottoming): +237bps/20d, +361bps/60d — BEST absolute, consistent with the contract's "prime entry" claim.
- Peak (Topping): +58bps/20d, +238bps/60d absolute, but NEGATIVE excess vs SPY: -39bps/20d, -72bps/60d — the "topping is bad" intuition is directionally real.
- BUT Peak-vs-nonPeak is NOT statistically significant: Welch t=-1.70 p=0.089 (20d), t=-1.00 p=0.316 (60d); excess t=-1.16 p=0.248 / t=-0.72 p=0.473. The edge is a soft tilt, not a gate.

PART B — does the veto improve the bot's actual leadership rule? NO. Walk-forward, monthly, top-4 RS sectors above 200d equal-weight, strict point-in-time:
- BASELINE:   CAGR 8.17%  Sharpe 0.61  maxDD -23.35%  (2.43x)
- PEAK-HALVE:  CAGR 6.54%  Sharpe 0.57  maxDD -22.76%  (2.05x)
- PEAK-EXCLUDE:CAGR 4.77%  Sharpe 0.47  maxDD -22.62%  (1.70x)
Vetoing Peak sectors monotonically DESTROYS return and Sharpe while cutting drawdown by <1pp. The reason: top-RS leaders are frequently IN the Peak phase precisely while they are still leading; halving/excluding them forfeits the leadership premium the sleeve exists to harvest.

PART C — robustness / other framings:
- VETO Peak+Downturn: CAGR 0.44%, Sharpe 0.11, but maxDD -12.24%. This halves drawdown ONLY by sitting in cash — pure de-grossing, exactly RC5's subtract-only pathology. Not risk-adjusted improvement (Sharpe collapses).
- CYCLE-TILT (additive/RC1 angle: overweight Trough/Recovery to 0.35, underweight Peak to 0.15): CAGR 7.29%, Sharpe 0.61 — matches baseline Sharpe, slightly lower CAGR. No improvement.
- Conditional on risk-off (SPY<200d, n=23 rebalances): base already earns +1.82%/mo; VETO-PK gives +1.87% (marginal) but costs risk-on months (+0.52%→+0.15%). The veto does not even earn its keep in the drawdown regime it's meant to protect.
- Context: SPY B&H CAGR 14.08% Sharpe 0.91; the user's SELF-DEF book (XLU/XLV/XLF/XLP EW) CAGR 9.45% Sharpe 0.76 — both beat every leadership variant on Sharpe, corroborating the user's framing that the defensive book outperforms.

CONFIDENCE-HAIRCUT variant (optional): SKIPPED honestly — the leadership sleeve consumes no regime-confidence input in this test and the contract's per-sector phase carries no stored confidence field, so a regime-confidence haircut cannot be cleanly attributed to the cycle signal without confounding it with a market-timing overlay. The Part-C conditional split (SPY-trend regime) is the closest clean proxy and showed no benefit.

PROXY VALIDATION: My oscillator/phase reconstruction is faithful — osc-position correlation 0.994 vs the live contract, 9/11 exact phase matches as of 2026-06-26 (2 mismatches are boundary direction-tiebreaks: XLK Peak-vs-Downturn, XLU Trough-vs-Recovery, from MACD-vs-osc-slope direction). Conclusion is not a proxy artifact. No look-ahead: osc uses only causal ewm/rolling(min_periods) ops; all rebalance quantities computed from close[:T].

NET FOR W2: The sector_cycles.json phase is a decent DESCRIPTIVE bottoming/topping map (Trough forward returns are genuinely strong) but a poor PRESCRIPTIVE veto for a momentum-leadership sleeve, because leaders live in Peak. If W2 ships at all, it should be (1) an ENTRY-side Trough/Recovery preference for NEW additions (the one leg with positive excess return and the additive RC1 flavor), NOT (2) a Peak exit/veto on existing leaders. Even the entry tilt only matched baseline Sharpe here, so the bar for building it is high.
resolutions.method: Faithful reimplementation of vendor/macro_src/engine/sector_cycles.py _detrended_osc (252d EMA-detrend, 252d stochastic min-max, ewm smooth) and _classify_phase (0-100 position + direction), validated against the live contract (corr 0.994, 9/11 phase match). Walk-forward 2015-2026 on dividend-adjusted sector-ETF parquets (data/yahoo/XL*.parquet, SPY), strict point-in-time (close[:T]). Part A: pooled sector-month forward 20d/60d returns by phase + Welch t-tests (excess vs SPY). Part B/C: monthly top-4 RS>200d EW leadership sleeve with base/halve/exclude/veto-Peak+Downturn/cycle-tilt variants; CAGR, annualized vol, Sharpe, maxDD; conditional split on SPY-vs-200d regime. Scripts under /tmp/mm_reaudit/.

PART A pooled N=1444: Trough f20=+237bps/f60=+361bps (best); Peak f20_ex=-39bps f60_ex=-72bps (negative alpha but Welch p=0.089/0.316 — not significant)
PART B walk-forward: BASELINE CAGR 8.17% Sharpe 0.61 maxDD -23.35% vs PEAK-EXCLUDE CAGR 4.77% Sharpe 0.47 maxDD -22.62% — veto monotonically worse
PART C: VETO Peak+Downturn CAGR 0.44% Sharpe 0.11 maxDD -12.24% = de-gross-to-cash (RC5), not alpha; CYCLE-TILT Sharpe 0.61 = no improvement over baseline

resolutions.implications: De-prioritize / redesign masterplan wave W2. The prior audit's implicit assumption — that sector_cycles.json is consumed by zero code (RC4) and wiring it in would add value — is only half right: consuming it as a Peak veto would ACTIVELY HARM the leadership sleeve and add yet another subtract-only cash lever (RC5), the exact pathology the re-audit is trying to escape. The empirically defensible use is narrow: an ENTRY-side preference for Trough/Recovery (Prime-entry) sectors on NEW additions only (the sole leg with positive excess return and an additive RC1 character), never a topping-exit on held leaders. Even that only matched baseline Sharpe, so W2 should either ship as this narrow entry tilt or be dropped in favor of higher-leverage work. It does NOT close the gap to the defensive self-directed book (Sharpe 0.76), which still beats every leadership variant — reinforcing that the real fix is rotation-into-defensives (RC5/RC6), not a cycle gate on momentum leaders. Falsification: re-run with a true weekly+3d MACD direction leg (not the osc-slope proxy) and daily rebalance; if a Peak veto then shows Sharpe > baseline+0.1 out-of-sample, revisit.

resolutions.headline: Arming MASTERMIND_FLAGSHIP_JUDGMENT produces a genuinely divergent book (rotates out of the ETF momentum sleeve into single names and holds ~29% cash) — echo-risk is LOW — but the divergence is blind to the contrarian signals (regime confidence/transition_state, froth/macro-risk, and the outperforming self-directed defensive book) because all three are stripped before the seats see them.
resolutions.answer:
DIVERGE, not echo — but the divergence is momentum-flavored, not contrarian-informed.

(1) INCENTIVE — divergence-friendly. brain/pm_conviction.py:99-126 (_PM_PERSONA) tells the PM: (a) "IDLE CASH EARNS ~4% ANNUALIZED ... holding cash when you lack high-conviction ideas is a REWARDED choice, not dead money" and "NEVER dilute the book with marginal names just to stay fully invested" — explicit permission to hold cash / not stay invested; (b) "EXPRESS EACH THEME THROUGH SINGLE NAMES, NOT ETFs. ... broad sector/index/factor ETFs (e.g. SMH, XLK, MTUM, IWM) are a LAST-RESORT placeholder ... must never be the core of the book" — explicit permission to rotate OUT of the engine's top-RS ETF leadership sleeve (the RC2 momentum funnel); (c) "you MAY add high-conviction thematic names the engine missed and DROP engine names that lack a live thesis"; (d) "Confirmation over prediction — every name needs a why-now." Grading is forward rel_return vs SPY, 21d (brain/calibration.py:32,55,114; brain/cio.py:57 vs="SPY"). A grep for press/winners/NAV/S&P over brain/*.py returns ONLY attribution/benchmark plumbing (attribution.py, decision.py, calibration.py) — there is NO "beat the S&P", "press your winners", "stay fully invested", or headline/NAV-race directive in any persona. The reward structure permits and rewards divergence.

(2) EMPIRICAL PROOF IT DIVERGES — the live dry-run artifact. data/portfolios/flagship_judgment/_pending_decision.json (written 2026-07-01 18:44, a real armed-Opus dry-run) shows the PM did NOT echo: it dropped IREN ("crowded high-beta"), TRIMMED the engine's core momentum ETFs SMH/XLK/MTUM ~2pts each explicitly "to respect the contracting-liquidity governor", kept IWM full as the "healthy broadening leg", RAISED EME to a real position, added ~18 single-name industrial/electrification names (EME/AME/APH/ANET/TILE/WAB/CHRW/FSS/NDSN/HUBB/MLI/DD/DY/KMT/LQDT/EXPD/MAS/GATX/URI), and held ~29% cash ("dry powder for the pullback the engine is telling me to wait for"). gross=0.704. It also explicitly DECLINED four Strategist-named "confirmed leaders" (AEIS/CAT/TLN/ETN) because they failed the engine gate. That is a book with a different sleeve mix, different names, and a large deliberate cash sleeve — the opposite of an echo.

(3) CONTRARIAN INPUTS — largely NOT fed (the caveat). The regime file (vendor/macro_src/data/regime/latest.json) HAS confidence=0.327, transition_state=WEAKENING, plus contradicting, froth_fragility, macro_risk, risk_state, turning_point. But every intake point strips them to the same 7-key bullish slice {quad, quad_name, growth_score, inflation_score, liquidity_overlay, cycle_tag, sector_rs_top}: strategist input brain/strategist.py:65-67, PM input brain/pm_conviction.py:85-87, and the get_regime MCP tool brain/bot_mcp.py:~130. So neither seat is told the regime is low-confidence (0.327) or WEAKENING/transitioning — the RC4 confidence-blind intake reproduces itself inside the judgment layer. The self-directed defensive book (XLU/XLV/XLF/XLP, the +1.45% benchmark the user says beats every model) is invisible: no MCP tool exposes it (grep for self-direct/defensive/XLU/XLV/XLP over brain/bot_mcp.py and brain/flagship_desk_mcp.py returns nothing), and read_signal (bot_mcp.py:477-496) actively DENIES reading any portfolio book. sector_cycles.json is only reachable if the PM proactively guesses the path and calls read_signal — it is not in the prompt. MACRO RISK OFFICER context (macro_rs state/fragility/gross_cap/defensive_tilt) IS injected into portfolio_ctx (judgment_book.py:191-193) but ONLY when MASTERMIND_MACRO_RISK=1 AND it feeds the deterministic subtract-only teeth, not the PM's idea generation. Net: the seats can diverge, but on the same bullish confirmed-theme funnel the engine uses — the divergence you get is "rotate momentum ETFs into single-name industrials + hold cash", not "the regime is weakening at 0.327 confidence, rotate to defensives" — because the defensive-relevant facts never enter the prompt.

(4) ANCHORING RISK — MODERATE. The PM sees the engine's WEIGHTS before opining: _pm_input embeds engine_candidates with "weight": c.get("weight") (brain/pm_conviction.py:56), serialized straight into the prompt JSON (brain/pm_conviction.py:129-157, _build_prompt dumps payload). It also sees the engine's per-name bull/bear and the Strategist's confirmed-theme list. There is no "reason from a blank book" framing. The 07-01 artifact shows the anchoring is not fatal (the PM re-weighted and dropped names), but weights-visible-first is a real anchor toward the engine's sizing, and the whole candidate pool is the engine's own funnel plus its rejected pool — the PM is not shown any independently-sourced defensive universe to anchor against.

(5) DEFINITIVE SHADOW A/B DESIGN.
  Env — SHADOW arm (never touches the live book; PM submits to the isolated flagship_judgment path per pm_conviction.py:30 + flagship_desk_mcp.py:12-13): MASTERMIND_FLAGSHIP_JUDGMENT=1, MASTERMIND_GATE_OFFICER=1, MASTERMIND_MACRO_RISK=1 (arm the defensive teeth so the A/B tests the FULL judgment stack), MASTERMIND_SELF_MIRROR=1, FLAGSHIP_PM_MAX_TURNS=30, MASTERMIND_RESEARCH_LLM=1. CONTROL arm = the current live engine book (flagship trunk, judgment OFF). Run both nightly on the SAME asof/regime so the only variable is the seat.
  Duration — min 25 trading nights to clear cio.py:_MIN_DATES=8 independent (thinned) clusters for a Newey-West t-stat; 40 nights preferred (the seats grade on a 21d horizon, so the first fully-resolved KPI window lands ~21 trading days in).
  Metrics, logged per night from the isolated flagship_judgment artifacts + nav_history.jsonl: (i) DIVERGENCE RATE = 1 - Jaccard(name set) and L1 weight distance between judgment book and engine book; (ii) CASH% of the judgment book (gross from _pending_decision.json); (iii) SEMIS/momentum-ETF weight = summed weight in {SMH,XLK,MTUM,SOXX,IWM,QQQ} — the RC2 crowded sleeve; (iv) single-name % vs ETF %; (v) NAV vs engine book AND vs SPY AND vs the self-directed defensive basket (equal-weight XLU/XLV/XLF/XLP) via cio._nav_summary (extend _NAV_BOOKS with a synthetic self-directed row); (vi) contrarian-alignment: correlation between judgment cash% and regime confidence/transition_state on days the regime WEAKENS.
  Success thresholds (echo-risk LOW confirmed): divergence rate > 0.30 name-Jaccard AND >8pts mean L1 weight distance across the window; momentum-ETF weight < engine's by >=5pts on average; cash% responds to regime (cash% on WEAKENING/low-confidence days materially above risk-on days). FAILURE / echo (would flip verdict to HIGH): divergence rate < 0.10, cash% flat ~engine, momentum-ETF weight within 2pts of engine. WIN condition (the point of the program): judgment NAV beats BOTH the engine book AND the self-directed defensive basket over the window with a Newey-West-significant PM KPI (cio.py per-seat significance, ci95 lower bound > 0). PARTIAL (diverges but doesn't beat defensives): expected given finding (3) — the fix is to feed confidence/transition_state/froth + a defensive universe into _pm_input/_strategist_input/get_regime, then re-run.
